comments.value:
It turns out I missed two important bits of information, so I've edited my main feedback post as well as my GitHub comment on Proton (linked in that feedback post):

#1 - Fresh Steam installations don't include the h264 video codec unlocked by default.  You have to run "steam steam://unlockh264" or such then restart Steam to enable the visual part of video playback in VRChat.

After including that step, I can recreate this crash in VRChat Desktop mode on both my normal computer and a lower-powered system as well.

#2 - Any substantial AVPro audio/video desync (e.g. VRChat stuttering) results in the Desktop mode crash on VRChat Open Beta with Proton Experimental, it doesn't need to be 100% CPU load.

On my normal computer, I may need to load all CPU cores to 100% and toggle on the personal mirror or switch avatars until VRChat media playback stutters enough to trigger the crash.

On a lower power system, I just had to toggle on personal mirror for the first time with the media playing, and that stutter was enough to trigger the crash.  And I was wearing the default Robot avatar, nothing heavy.

(NOTE₁: In my limited testing, the Unity media player - e.g. as in the "iY MMD World" - has recovered from stuttering without crashing, even on VRChat Open Beta with Proton Experimental.)

(NOTE₂: VR mode appears to trigger this audio/video desync crash without requiring any special effort other than the AVPro player beginning playback in the Talent Show world.)

With the recent stable release of VRChat 2023.3.3p1, this crash now happens on VRChat stable, and with Proton 8.x!

So.. technically, this is no longer specific to Open Beta, and it might happen with the stock Steam Deck configuration (unfortunately, I do not have a Steam Deck to test - it is a bit dependent on CPU load/availability).

I've posted a new comment to Valve's Proton issue tracker with VRChat & Proton debug logs for all 8 tested combinations:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1770336669

On a stock Steam Deck (default Proton, default h264 - not sure if it's unlocked by default on Deck - developer mode enabled), plus the stable version of VRC, I wasn't able to cause a crash in this world with video playing with the mirror or loading a Very Poor non-cached avatar - but I was able to cause one by taking a 4K photo.

I can upload the output log from /home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/438100/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/LocalLow/VRChat/VRChat/ or the crash.dmp file somewhere if needed but the uploader here only seems to support images.

QM build: 1370

Good news!  The root cause of this issue has been tracked down to a race condition in Proton, and there's an open pull request to 'dxvk' to fix it.  I've built a custom Proton version featuring the 'dxvk' patch and it has solved the crashing issues for me, as documented here:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1813844933

As this *should* be fixed whenever Valve merges in the 'dxvk' code change to Proton and releases that in an update, you can probably mark this feedback entry as fixed.

Dear VRChat employee,

I truly hope you can see and enjoy how much you have helped people care for each other. There are a lot of friends I like to play with, and they have settled on VRChat. As such, I very much want to play on VRChat in order to play with my friends. While the product you have made still has a long way to go, many modelers and scripters have worked together with optimizing programmers towards helping make the wonderous ability to show yourself to others how you want to be in worlds where they want to go. This is a very powerful feature, and I really hope you can get closer. There is clearly a lot of love in the community for helping each other have a lot of fun and comfort. Please, do everything you can to support them, and be careful to make sure you give them room to explore. The mod ban hit them hard, even if you had good intentions.

As a Linux user, however, I have run into more issues than most. Some updates, I have to figure out some combination of SteamVR version and Proton version to get VRC to even launch. Some releases, it seems to work fine on all of them. One recurring issue that has been getting worse, though, is the crashing worlds. I believe it is some video players crashing me constantly.

Via ProtonDB, ( https://www.protondb.com/app/438100 ), in a post titled "AVPro video players don't work", I am offered a launch option "--disable-hw-video-decoding". This seems to fix the crashing worlds. I still miss out on video in those worlds which can severly limit what I am able to get from them, but there were worlds that still used a video player where I could see and hear what is seen and heard by those around me. As of late, however, the last I knew of them no longer work.

Two beautiful worlds with video players that used to work for me and no longer work at all for me are linked.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_93dc2a1f-60f6-474f-ba8b-f86ad2fd8025

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_3d892cf2-cd4a-4322-9e7e-2ec0cd7ea44c

While older versions of the worlds worked just fine, that is no longer the case for me. Without the launch option, those places crash me, not even letting me play with the rest of what is there.

Right now, there is one scenario where I see even partial functionality. When I join the world, I get to hear music. When I check the video player and show its controls, I see that the mode "Stream" is selected. When I try "Video" mode, it fails to work as all the other players, but the audio-only stream seems to function just fine.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_65ce4a4b-f66f-4844-adfe-072663394514

I know you may not consider Linux support as a priority issue, but when you see how a company that traps you onto their platform can wantonly mistreat the people you love and keep getting away with it, you may very well know the pain of loss and the desire to build a better future that comes with it. I have personally taken this as a way to try making sure that, for the next wave of people left marooned by a company that thinks they own your experience, there will be a safe, comfortable, and productive place where they can continue being themselves. I know you do not want anyone to feel trapped on your platform, and that you are dealing with your early design decisions and plenty of other issues I am sure I do not know. For my own use, though, I really just want the option to relax with my friends and watch something together. If this is an easy enough fix, it would go a long way towards letting all the other Linux users play without having to go to an external site to find the fix and put in a launch option in a realm of worlds devoid of that bit of life.

Thank you and well wishes,

Green_Dragon_Iris

details:
I have commented on Valve's VRChat issue with full details including VRChat and Proton logs.  I'm reporting it here as well since it is specific to the Open Beta:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1732524122

2023-10-4 update: Steam does not enable h264 decoding by default!  You'll need to manually enable this if the video portion of the audiovisual stream does not show.

2023-10-19 update: With VRChat 2023.3.3p1 stable release, this crash now impacts VRChat stable, and it crashes on Proton 8.x, too!  I've posted a new comment to Valve's VRChat issue with all the test results and debug logs:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1770336669

2023-10-20 update: VRChat now disables AVPro by default on Linux.  You can pass "--enable-avpro-in-proton" to the Steam launch properties to continue testing.

Steps:

1.  Set up SteamVR on Linux (tested with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, HTC Vive, AMD RX 5600 XT)

2.  Make sure h264 video codec is unlocked in Steam, e.g. by running "steam steam://unlockh264"

3.  Install VRChat

4.  Configure VRChat properties to force "Proton Experimental" as the compatibility tool (to work around audio blasting at 100%, a recent Proton 8.0 stable regression)

5.  Load the Show Talents game world in VR: https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_20f170b0-57b4-4673-a8a7-329ebc07e047

6.  Walk towards stage, wait for video to load

7. If on desktop, do something to cause VRChat audio/video playback to stutter (e.g. taking a 4K photo with the camera, loading the CPU, toggling on personal mirror, switching avatars)

8.  Crash

Please see the linked Valve issue tracker for the full test matrix - VRChat open beta crashes crashes on VR and desktop (with some effort); VRChat stable works in both situations.

I realize this issue may be in Valve's court; this feedback post can be closed if so.

Last retested: 2023-10-19

 * VRChat QM build: 1370

 * Proton Experimental: 1697215757 experimental-8.0-20231011b
